removed_issues.title: Verify .bvvi index byte-compat against a real Go-written index file
removed_issues.description:
TUI_UX_PARITY_PLAN.md §14 item 4 shipped a new `bv-search::vector_index` module (crates/bv-search/src/vector_index.rs) that implements the `.bvvi` binary format byte-for-byte per Go pkg/search/vector_index.go (magic "BVVI", version 1 LE, header magic[4]+version u16+reserved u16+dim u32+count u32, per-entry id_len u16+id+sha256[32]+dim*f32 LE). All validation bounds were ported (max dim 2^20, max entries 2^20, max file 512MiB, duplicate-id reject, trailing-data reject) and round-trip tests exist (save then load through the Rust side only).

What was explicitly NOT verified (see the §14 "Explicitly not done" list): whether an index file *actually written by the Go binary* loads correctly in Rust, and vice versa. The current tests only prove the Rust encoder and Rust decoder agree with each other — a structural format match on paper is not the same as a verified interop test.

Why this matters: if bvr and the Go bv ever run against the same project directory (shared .bv/semantic/index-hash-<dim>.bvvi path — see bv_search::index_sync::default_index_path), a subtly wrong byte offset or endianness assumption would silently corrupt the shared index or cause one binary to reject the others output. This is exactly the kind of bug that never shows up in same-language round-trip tests.

Acceptance criteria:
1. Install the users local Go bv (v0.24.1, already on PATH per prior session — `go install github.com/Dicklesworthstone/beads_viewer/cmd/bv@latest`) and run `bv --search "<query>" --search-mode hybrid` (or whatever CLI flag builds the semantic index) against a small fixture repo to produce a real `.bv/semantic/index-hash-<dim>.bvvi` file written by Go.
2. Load that file with `bv_search::vector_index::VectorIndex::load()` in a new integration test (crates/bv-search/tests/ or a #[test] in vector_index.rs marked to only run when a fixture file is committed) and assert the entries/dims/hashes match what `bv --robot-search` reports for the same query.
3. Conversely, write a `.bvvi` file with the Rust encoder over the same fixture and confirm the Go binary loads it without error (may require a small Go-side smoke script since we cannot call Go code from Rust tests directly — documenting the manual verification steps + a committed fixture file/checksum is an acceptable substitute for full CI automation if a live Go binary is not available in CI).
4. If a real incompatibility is found, fix crates/bv-search/src/vector_index.rs (not the Go side) and add a regression test with the exact byte sequence that broke.
5. If everything round-trips cleanly, commit the Go-generated fixture `.bvvi` file under crates/bv-search/tests/fixtures/ (or similar) and a test that loads it, so future changes to vector_index.rs get a real cross-binary regression guard instead of just same-language round-trip coverage.

Not in scope: rebuilding the whole semantic search TUI wiring (already done in §14 item 4) — this bead is purely about the file-format interop guarantee.

If cass IS available, press V on a bead with known correlated sessions, confirm the modal shows real session cards, j/k navigation moves the highlighted session, y copies the search command (paste it somewhere to confirm), and V/Esc/Enter/q all close the modal.

removed_issues.title: Cass modal timestamp correlation strategy (Go's third strategy, currently scope-cut)
removed_issues.description:
crates/bv-tui/src/cass.rs ports Go pkg/cass/correlation.go Correlator.Correlate strategy order as: id-mention search first, then keywords search over title+description if id-mention finds nothing. Gos actual Correlator has a third strategy this port explicitly skips: StrategyTimestamp ("Matched via: recent activity timeframe" in formatMatchReason), which correlates sessions purely by being active during the beads open window (calculateSearchDays: for closed issues, the window between creation and closure + a 7-day buffer; for open issues, time since creation capped at 90 days).

Why it was skipped (see cass.rs module doc comment): the timestamp strategy in Go needs session-mtime metadata from the cass indexs internal state that this Rust port does not parse — the Rust backend only shells out to `cass search <query> --robot --limit N` and reads the JSON `results[]` array (source_path/line_number/agent/title/score/snippet/timestamp/match_type), which does not include a way to query "all sessions active in window [start,end] regardless of text query match." Implementing this would need either (a) a new cass CLI flag/mode this port cannot assume exists, or (b) parsing cass raw session index files directly (undocumented format, high risk of drift).

Investigate before implementing:
1. Check the *currently installed* cass CLI (`cass --help`, `cass search --help`) for a date/time-range-only query mode that does not require search terms — Go may already be relying on a flag like `--days N` combined with an empty or wildcard query, which this port could reuse without needing new cass features. Read pkg/cass/search.go `buildArgs` again (already read once this session — see `Search.buildArgs`: `--days` is passed today when opts.Days > 0, but always alongside a keyword query, so check whether an EMPTY `opts.Query` with `--days` set returns "everything active in that window" or errors/no-ops).
2. If cass supports empty-query + --days, port `calculateSearchDays` (crates/bv-tui/src/cass.rs, alongside `extract_keywords`) and add a third correlate() fallback: after id-mention and keywords both come up empty, try a days-only search.
3. If cass does NOT support this, document that finding clearly in a code comment (update the existing scope-cut comment in cass.rs to say WHY, not just THAT it is skipped) and close this bead as wont-fix with that reasoning recorded — do not invent undocumented cass index-file parsing to work around a missing CLI feature.

Acceptance: either (a) timestamp strategy implemented + tested (unit test with a fixture issue open/closed window + mocked cass output), or (b) bead closed with a documented, verified reason why it cannot be done without cass CLI changes outside this repos control.

removed_issues.title: FORT EPIC: Compatible Rust Successor of beads_viewer
removed_issues.description:

GOAL: Keep everything the bv agent ecosystem depends on byte-compatible (robot JSON schemas, CLI behavior incl. argv rewriting, exit codes 0/1/2, data_hash algorithm, issue semantics, export formats), then build a better engine underneath: cleaner crates, lower memory (target <=70% Go RSS), incremental analysis (v2), stronger agent API (v2).

TWO TRACKS (never mix in one change):
- FORT v1 = Phases 0-8: parity. Drop-in replacement verified by differential testing against frozen Go goldens.
- FORT v2 = Phases 9-10: native upgrades, strictly additive-only schema changes.

KEY STRATEGIC ASSETS:
1. crates/bv-graph-wasm/ = VERBATIM copy (diff -r verified) of Go repo's bv-graph-wasm @ 9ace029: 6,940 LOC Rust already implementing PageRank/HITS/eigenvector/betweenness exact+approx/k-core/articulation/cycles/critical-path/slack/topo/reachability/what-if/top-k. ~70% of graph engine work is extraction, not rewrite.

3. Frozen Go binary + golden outputs serve as the acceptance oracle for every phase.

removed_issues.title: Phase 1b: datasource discovery + SQLite reader + GitLoader as-of
removed_issues.description:
Plan §4.2 discovery + readers. Gate: part of CP-A.

DISCOVERY CHAIN (exact priority): BEADS_DB env (file->parent dir; ext .jsonl/.db/.sqlite/.sqlite3) > BEADS_DIR env > <repo>/.beads > main-repo .beads via worktree resolution (git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir; main root = parent of common dir).
- .beads/redirect follow: max 4096 bytes, depth 10; loop/non-UTF8/bad-target = ERROR; target must be dir named .beads/_beads.
- File pick among *.jsonl: exclude *.backup|.orig|.merge|deletions.jsonl|beads.left*|beads.right* (merge artifacts warn); preferred order [issues.jsonl, beads.jsonl, beads.base.jsonl], first preferred with size>0 wins; bd/Dolt workspace detection (.beads/dolt/|embeddeddolt/|metadata backend==dolt) NEVER falls back to stray non-issue JSONL (#189).
- SQLite reader: rusqlite read-only DSN; column/table presence probing for issues/dependencies/comments/labels (schema variance across br versions).
- GitLoader (--as-of): git rev-parse --verify resolve; on failure date layouts [RFC3339, YYYY-MM-DD, YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM, YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS] local tz -> git rev-list -1 --before=<RFC3339> HEAD; SHA-keyed cache TTL 5min with RWMutex-equivalent (RwLock), deep clone semantics on get/set, lazy eviction. Content via git show <sha>:<path> over the 3 preferred paths. Source selection priority SQLite=100 > worktree=80 > local=50, freshest mtime first, ties by priority.

removed_issues.title: Phase 1a: bv-core model types + JSONL tolerant parser
removed_issues.description:
Plan §4.1+§4.2 parse half. Gate: CP-A + CP-B.

MODEL (bv-core::model):
- Issue 25 fields, exact serde renames matching Go JSON tags. Status enum 10 values: open/in_progress/blocked/deferred/draft/pinned/hooked/review/closed/tombstone. IssueType: any non-empty valid (Gastown extensibility); known set epic/feature/bug/task/chore/docs/question kept separately for sort/icon. DependencyType blocks/related/parent-child/discovered-from; CRITICAL: empty string AND blocks both blocking (legacy compat — #[default] + custom deser). Validate(): ID+Title non-empty, Status in enum, reject updated_at<created_at.
- v1 uses plain String IDs for hash/deser parity; newtype IDs deferred to Phase 9 (v2).

PARSER (tolerant JSONL):
- BOM strip line 1 only. 10MB/line buffer default (BV_MAX_LINE_SIZE_MB env). Skip malformed lines + warn; never crash on garbage (merge-conflict reality).
- _type record routing: memory/sprint/forecast/burndown -> silent skip (counted in ParseStats.skipped); unknown _type -> skipped; no _type or issue -> parse as issue.
- Parallel parse gate: >=4MiB AND >=512 lines, 64KiB chunks x3 per worker via rayon; warnings replayed in GLOBAL line order; byte-identical results vs serial path.
- Validation gates: MaxJSONLErrorRate 0.10 reject threshold; reject Valid==0 && Errors+Skipped>0 (all-non-issue file); tombstone filter post-load; validation cache keyed path+mtime+size.
- LoadReport{path,valid,errors,skipped,warnings(<=10)} recorded process-global for envelope load_stats.

ACCEPTANCE (=CP-A/CP-B): field-level diff vs Go == 0 on all fixture classes incl. malformed mixes; data_hash byte-equal on every fixture (incl. edge cases); load_stats identical when records dropped.

removed_issues.title: Phase 10b: explainable scoring + richer agent API (capabilities/streaming/fast-mode)
removed_issues.description:
Plan §6 Phase 10b — richer agent API, strictly ADDITIVE schema changes (v1 goldens must pass unchanged).

EXPLAINABLE SCORING: optional reasons[] on recommendations/quick_ref entries — human+agent readable strings like 'blocks 14 issues', 'high pagerank 0.31', 'stale 20 days'. Derived from existing breakdown components (impact weights, triage factors). Optional fields only; consumers ignoring them see identical v1 behavior.

CAPABILITIES DECLARATION: version/envelope gains capabilities:[...] e.g. ['incremental-analysis','streaming','explain-score'] so agents can feature-detect. bv --robot-capabilities extended accordingly.

STREAMING ROBOT MODE: NDJSON streaming variant (--stream flag or content-type) emitting records progressively for large outputs (insights full_stats, history reports) — agents on slow links benefit; classic buffered output remains default and untouched.

FAST MODE: opt-in env (BV_FAST_MODE=1) enabling Phase 9 fast paths (parallel/zero-copy/incremental) with documented behavioral notes; compatibility mode stays default and golden-pinned.

PLUGIN ARCHITECTURE EXPLORATION: sketch-level only after the above land (recipe hooks? external analyzers?) — explicit non-goal to design it during v1/v2 parity work.

ACCEPTANCE: all FORT v1 goldens pass byte-identical with new binary (additive-only verified by CI assertion); new features demonstrated in docs/examples agent workflow.

removed_issues.title: Phase 10a: incremental analysis engine (affected-subgraph metric refresh)
removed_issues.description:
Plan §6 Phase 10a — THE killer feature a pure port cannot offer.

CONCEPT: beads change frequently (1 issue edit); today full graph recompute runs. Instead:
changed nodes -> affected subgraph closure -> update only affected metrics -> merge into cached GraphStats.

BUILD ON: existing dataHash keying, config-hash cache keys, LRU disk caches (Phase 2c foundation).

DESIGN SKETCH:
- Dirty-set propagation via dependency edges (forward dependents closure for centrality invalidation; SCC-aware when cycles present).
- PageRank incremental: retain previous vector as warm start with tighter iteration budget; fall back to full compute on divergence beyond 1e-9.
- Betweenness: exact incremental is hard — approximate refresh on affected component + flag status=approx with reason 'incremental'.
- Triage scores: cheap recompute from updated metrics maps (weights are local per-node).
- data_hash stays FULL-graph (contract!) — incremental affects internal caching layers only, never the envelope hash semantics.
- Expose metrics freshness in robot meta (phase2_ready semantics preserved; additive fields only e.g. incremental:true).

ACCEPTANCE: single-issue-edit refresh measured >=5x faster than full recompute on 10k fixture; outputs converge to full-compute values within tolerance; all v1 goldens still pass unchanged.

removed_issues.title: Phase 2b: two-phase analyzer + timeouts + MetricStatus
removed_issues.description:
Plan §4.3 two-phase analyzer.

DESIGN (mirrors Go goroutine+select):
- Phase1 synchronous: degree, topo sort, density — always immediately available.
- Phase2: one std::thread per metric with channel recv_timeout mirroring per-metric budgets from ConfigForSize (2s small / 500ms medium / 300ms large / 200ms XL for PR+HITS+Cycles; BW exact 2s/500ms, approx 500ms). Panic inside thread -> MetricStatus=timeout (catch_unwind at thread boundary). AllPhase2Disabled short-circuit when env BV_SKIP_PHASE2 set (disables PR/BW/HITS/cycles/eigenvector/critical-path; KEEPS k-core/articulation/slack).
- Env override BV_PHASE2_TIMEOUT_S=N (>0) replaces per-metric timeouts.
- GraphStats carries per-metric MetricStatus {computed|approx|timeout|skipped|pending|panic} + elapsed ms (+sample size when approx).

ACCEPTANCE: status flags identical to Go across fixture sizes incl. pathological graphs (dense complete graphs forcing skips); elapsed-ms ignored in diff; metrics maps equal at 1e-12.

removed_issues.title: Phase 2c: disk cache v3 + ConfigForSize + scoring constants
removed_issues.description:
Plan §4.3 cache + config + scoring constants.

DISK CACHE v3 (keep Go design, replace format+filename to avoid cross-binary misreads):
- Gated: BV_ROBOT=1 && BV_NO_CACHE!=1. Dir: $BV_CACHE_DIR else UserCacheDir()/bv.
- Key dataHash16|configHash16. Bounds: 24h age, 10 entries LRU, 10MB entry cap.
- .beads dir mtime staleness check invalidates. XFetch beta=1.0 probabilistic early refresh.
- Columnar SoA shape (nodes dictionary + set/idx/vals arrays).
- File locking fs2/fd-lock (flock unix / LockFileEx windows); no-rewrite-on-pure-read-hit; persist-only-fresh (never write after a git failure).
- In-proc TTL cache 5min global alongside disk layer.

CONFIG TIERS ConfigForSize(nodeCount,edgeCount) verbatim: density = E/(N*(N-1)); <100 nodes -> everything exact 2s timeouts, MaxCycles 1000; <500 -> exact 500ms, MaxCycles 100; <2000 -> 300ms, BW approx only if density<0.01 else skip reason 'graph too dense', MaxCycles 50; >=2000 -> BW approx always 500ms, PR 200ms, cycles DISABLED reason '>2000 nodes' MaxCycles 10, HITS only if density<0.001 else skipped.

SCORING CONSTANTS (copied): impact weights PR .22/BW .20/blocker .13/staleness .05/priority .10/TTI .10/urgency .10/risk .10 (risk=fan .30 churn .30 crossrepo .20 status .20); scoreToPriority >=.7->P0 >=.5->P1 >=.3->P2 >=.15->P3 else P4; TriageScore = base*0.70 + unblockBoost(<=0.15 threshold 5) + quickWin(<=0.15 depth<=2), claimed-by-other x0.1; QuickWin = log2(unblocks+1)*.4 + simplicity*.4 + prioBonus*.2; priority rec thresholds HighPageRank>.30 HighBetweenness>.50 staleness 14d minConfidence .30 significantDelta .15.

ACCEPTANCE: triage scores/reasons identical to Go on goldens (CP-C once wired through bv-robot); cache hit/miss behavior identical (timings ignored).

removed_issues.title: Phase 2a: bv-analysis import algorithms from wasm copy + Go-semantics alignment
removed_issues.description:
Plan §4.3. PARITY FIRST, PRETTY LATER.

Import algorithm modules DIRECTLY from crates/bv-graph-wasm (verbatim copy @9ace029): pagerank, hits, eigenvector, betweenness(+approx w/ recommend_sample_size), kcore, articulation+bridges, cycles(tarjan_scc + enumerate + cycle_break), critical_path, slack, topo, reachability, subgraph, whatif, topk_set, parallel_cut. Module paths and feature gates preserved; ONLY the wasm-bindgen dependency severed at boundary. NO bv-graph-core restructuring — that is Phase 9 after CP-F (every pre-parity graph refactor adds a variable against the Go oracle).

GO-SEMANTICS ALIGNMENTS REQUIRED (the only permitted code changes):
- PageRank: damp 0.85, tol 1e-6, maxIter 1000, deterministic power iteration (Go hand-rolled version semantics).
- HITS: tol 1e-3 replicating gonum network.HITS iteration/convergence behavior.
- Eigenvector: FIXED 50 iterations, no convergence check (Go behavior).
- Cycles: Tarjan SCC pre-check then one DFS cycle per SCC, capped by MaxCyclesToStore, sorted output.
- Slack: longest - fwd - bwd DP over topo order.
- Topo sort: Kahn with SORTED frontier (BTreeSet) — petgraph toposort order is unspecified; gonum topo.Sort determinism must be reproduced.
- Betweenness approx: Fisher-Yates seed=1, scale n/k; RecommendSampleSize tiers: <100->n exact, <500->max(50,n/5), <2000->100, else 200.
- k-core Batagelj-Zaversnik; articulation Tarjan undirected.
- Union-find for plan tracks: path compression + smaller-root-wins merge (determinism).

FLOAT DETERMINISM: all aggregations iterate in sorted node-index order; differential tolerance 1e-12 on robot-insights metrics maps.

removed_issues.title: Phase 3a: bv-robot CLI surface + validation rules + argv rewriter

removed_issues.title: TUI-M4: background worker + live reload infrastructure (week 7)
removed_issues.description:
Plan §6 Phase 6 TUI-M4 (week 7). Infrastructure week — behavioral parity with Go background mode.

WORKER THREAD DESIGN (std::thread + crossbeam-channel replacing goroutine+chan):
- Constants (env-overridable): debounce 200ms BV_DEBOUNCE_MS; message buffer 8 BV_CHANNEL_BUFFER; heartbeat 5s BV_HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL_S; watchdog 10s BV_WATCHDOG_INTERVAL_S; heartbeat-timeout 30s; freshness warn 30s BV_FRESHNESS_WARN_S / stale 120s BV_FRESHNESS_STALE_S; worker poll tick 120ms driving spinner; idle GC enabled.
- Pipeline: file event -> debounce -> load+validate -> Phase1 metrics sync in worker -> Phase2 async per-metric -> immutable DataSnapshot assembled -> ArcSwap pointer-swap to UI.
- Messages: SnapshotReadyMsg{snapshot,file_change_at,sent_at,version,queue_depth,coalesce_count} | SnapshotErrorMsg{err,recoverable} | Phase2UpdateMsg{data_hash}.
- Stale-drop: Phase2UpdateMsg with data_hash != current snapshot dropped.
- Snapshot swap protocol: capture selected IDs (list+board), clear attention overlay, exit time-travel, O(1) swap, return old pooled allocations, reset caches (label health/attention/drilldown/priority hints), recompute alerts + reset dismissals, semantic cache reset + optional hybrid rebuild, update sub-views preserving selection/recipe (applyRecipe vs direct ListItems when RecipeName+Hash match).
- Self-heal watchdog: repeated error phases shown as 'bg <phase> (Nx)'; watchdog recovery counter 'recovered xN'; unresponsive detection 'worker unresponsive'.
- Status indicators: fresh-age warning at 30s '⚠ 45s ago'; STALE at 120s; spinner frames while busy.
- Live reload: notify watcher watching FILE'S DIRECTORY with basename filter (atomic-rename reliability); remote-FS detect -> PollWatcher fallback (BV_FORCE_POLLING/BV_FORCE_POLL force); poll interval 2s comparing mtime+size+existence.
- ctrl+r/F5 force refresh 1s-throttled.

ACCEPTANCE: edit .beads/issues.jsonl externally -> list updates without restart <1s; kill -STOP worker -> watchdog indicators appear then recover on SIGCONT.
